extracted.intended_audience: covered entities (health care providers, issuers, State Exchanges), OCR compliance officers, legal counsel, accessibility/language services coordinators
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts the definitional standards and operational requirements under HHS OCR's final rule implementing Section 1557, including qualifications for interpreters/translators/readers, assurances, remedial/voluntary actions, and coordinator designation for covered entities.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified interpreter for an individual with a disability
rubrics_metrics.description: An interpreter who, via a video remote interpreting service (VRI) or an on-site appearance: (1) has demonstrated proficiency in communicating in, and understanding: (i) both English and a non-English language (including American Sign Language, other sign languages); or (ii) another communication modality (such as cued-language transliterators or oral transliteration); (2) is able to interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially, both receptively and expressively, using any necessary specialized vocabulary or terms without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving the tone, sentiment, and emotional level of the original statement; and (3) adheres to generally accepted interpreter ethics principles including client confidentiality. Qualified interpreters include, for example, sign language interpreters, oral transliterators, and cued-language transliterators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Definition aligns with prior rules and was revised to be consistent with the definition for LEP interpreters. OCR declines to require certification as a mandated element of this definition, but will consider certification in compliance assessments. Covered entities must ensure anyone designated to serve as an interpreter meets this definition and the unique needs of the individual. Use of VRI is explicitly included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified interpreter for an individual with limited English proficiency (LEP)
rubrics_metrics.description: An interpreter who via a remote interpreting service or an on-site appearance: (1) has demonstrated proficiency in speaking and understanding both spoken English and at least one other spoken language (qualified interpreters for relay interpretation must demonstrate proficiency in two non-English spoken languages); (2) is able to interpret effectively, accurately, and impartially to and from such language(s) and English (or between two non-English languages for relay interpretation), using any necessary specialized vocabulary or terms without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving the tone, sentiment, and emotional level of the original oral statement; and (3) adheres to generally accepted interpreter ethics principles, including client confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR revised this definition to permit relay interpretation where necessary for languages of limited diffusion (e.g., indigenous languages), while noting relay interpretation can introduce accuracy challenges. Interpreter must be proficient in languages required by role (including two non-English languages if serving as relay interpreter). Certification is not required in the definition but may be considered.

rubrics_metrics.name: Relay interpretation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreting from one language to another through an intermediate language: the first interpreter listens to the speaker and renders the message into the intermediate language; the second interpreter receives the message in the intermediate language and interprets it into a third language for the speaker who speaks neither the first nor the second language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recognized as an acceptable mode for monolingual speakers of languages of limited diffusion when direct interpretation to/from English is unavailable after reasonable efforts. OCR acknowledges relay interpretation may introduce accuracy concerns but permits it to afford meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified translator (written)
rubrics_metrics.description: A translator who: (1) has demonstrated proficiency in writing and understanding both written English and at least one other written non-English language; (2) is able to translate effectively, accurately, and impartially to and from such language(s) and English, using any necessary specialized vocabulary or terms without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving the tone, sentiment, and emotional level of the original written statement; and (3) adheres to generally accepted translator ethics principles, including client confidentiality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This definition is carried forward from prior rules. OCR declines to mandate certification or a specific assessment process in the definition, but will consider certification and other evidence in compliance assessments. OCR also notes that reasonable steps to provide meaningful access may require both written translation and oral interpreting for complex communications.

rubrics_metrics.name: Qualified reader
rubrics_metrics.description: A person who is able to read effectively, accurately, and impartially using any necessary specialized vocabulary.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Added for clarity (source: ADA regulations). OCR finalized this definition without modification; it clarifies expectations when a reader is required under the regulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Certification and licensure not required as minimum standard
rubrics_metrics.description: OCR declines to require certification or to incorporate State licensure requirements as a minimum standard for the definition of 'qualified interpreter' or 'qualified translator.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR will take certification and licensure into account in assessing compliance and covered entities may use State licensure as a means to demonstrate compliance where licensure demonstrates the individual possesses the definitional requirements. However, due to variability and lack of certifications for many languages, certification is not mandated in the rule text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of staff-as-interpreters limitation
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities must not use the services of staff who use sign language or another communication modality to act as interpreters and relay information to individuals with disabilities unless those staff meet the definition of 'qualified interpreter for an individual with a disability' and meet the unique needs of the individual.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The rule's definition addresses the concern; anyone designated by a covered entity to serve as an interpreter must be qualified per the definition. This reinforces that ad hoc use of unqualified staff is not acceptable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inclusion of remote/video interpreting services
rubrics_metrics.description: Definitions of qualified interpreter and qualified interpreter services include interpretation 'via a video remote interpreting service (VRI)' or other remote interpreting services.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR explicitly accepts telehealth and remote interpreting modalities (including video remote interpreting) as valid delivery mechanisms for interpreter services and considers them within the scope of meaningful access requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Preservation of tone, sentiment, and emotional level in interpretation/translation
rubrics_metrics.description: Interpreters and translators must interpret/translate using necessary specialized vocabulary without changes, omissions, or additions and while preserving the tone, sentiment, and emotional level of the original statement (oral or written).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Commenters emphasized this requirement to avoid altered meaning; OCR affirms this standard as part of the core qualifications for interpreters/translators to ensure accurate and faithful communication.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reasonable steps may require combined services
rubrics_metrics.description: Reasonable steps to provide meaningful access may require the provision of both written translation and oral interpreting.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR notes that for complex or technical communications (e.g., medical terminology), written translations alone may be insufficient and combined use of qualified translators and interpreters may be necessary to ensure comprehension and meaningful access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'telehealth'
rubrics_metrics.description: Telehealth means the use of electronic information and telecommunications technologies to support long-distance clinical health care, patient and professional health-related education, public health, and health administration. Technologies include videoconferencing, the internet, store-and-forward imaging, streaming media, and terrestrial and wireless communications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Included to clarify coverage under the rule; telehealth modalities are within scope for providing communication/access services (e.g., remote interpreting). Definition aligns with HRSA and ONC references.

rubrics_metrics.name: Definition of 'State' for rule purposes
rubrics_metrics.description: State means each of the several States, the District of Columbia, the Commonwealth of Puerto Rico, Guam, American Samoa, the Virgin Islands, the Trust Territory of the Pacific Islands, and the Commonwealth of the Northern Mariana Islands.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Finalized to avoid confusion about jurisdictional coverage; consistent with ADA regulations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assurances of compliance required (§92.5)
rubrics_metrics.description: Each entity applying for Federal financial assistance, each issuer seeking certification to participate in an Exchange, and each State seeking approval to operate a State Exchange is required to submit an assurance that its health programs and activities will be operated in compliance with section 1557 and this part.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Duration of obligation and covenants language adopt corresponding requirements in section 504 regulation (45 CFR 84.5). OCR declined proposals to add demographic data-collection or require applicants to submit budgets/policies explaining how they will provide language assistance services in the assurances provision; those obligations are addressed elsewhere in the rule.

rubrics_metrics.name: Remedial and voluntary action requirements (§92.6)
rubrics_metrics.description: Recipients or State Exchanges found by the Director to have engaged in discriminatory conduct must take remedial action to redress harms and may be required to take voluntary actions to remediate effects of discrimination; where a recipient exercises control over another recipient that has discriminated, either or both entities may be required to take remedial action. Covered entities may voluntarily take nondiscriminatory steps to overcome effects that limited participation in programs or activities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Remedial action is required only after a finding of discrimination and is tailored to the facts of the case (OCR draws on past resolution agreements for examples). Voluntary actions remain discretionary and OCR declines to convert voluntary duties into mandatory ones. OCR also declines to require covered entities to notify participants about findings and remedial actions, though OCR may publicize enforcement actions itself.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of 'control' and obligations of controlling entities
rubrics_metrics.description: Where a recipient exercises control over another recipient that has discriminated, the Director may require either or both entities to take remedial action.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The concept of 'control' has longstanding meaning in civil rights regulations; OCR declines to redefine it here. Whether a controlling entity must act will depend on established principles and the facts of the case.

rubrics_metrics.name: Designation of a Section 1557 Coordinator (§92.7)
rubrics_metrics.description: Covered entities with 15 or more employees are required to designate at least one employee to serve as a Section 1557 Coordinator to coordinate efforts to comply with and carry out the covered entity's responsibilities under section 1557; covered entities may assign one or more designees as appropriate.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OCR sought comment on whether smaller entities should be required to designate coordinators but finalized the 15+ employee threshold. Commenters strongly supported the Coordinator requirement as a means to address ignorance/administrative indifference and to support implementation, especially for small or rural entities. OCR may provide training and support for Coordinators.
